rules: Only `state` may be sent to the model under test. `meta` and `expected` (including `expected.rationale`, which names the real CVE/CWE) are harness-only and must never be included in a Jev/Noul prompt or a free-agent's context.
No CVE ID, advisory text, or fix commit in `state`.
diff_items carry package name and resolved versions only -- no summaries. A one-line summary drawn from release notes or commit bodies would itself be the level-3 hint (CIT-280 review, section 2).

files holds the full generator-produced new_framework_defaults_7_0.rb verbatim, not a hand-picked subset, so every Rails 7.0 default flip competes equally and variant_processor is not pre-highlighted (CIT-280 review, section 2).

expected.low: all others (a01, a04, a07, a08, a09, a10)

rationale.a02_security_misconfiguration: Ground truth: the public advisory maps this CVE to CWE-1188, Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default -- Active Storage did not disable libvips's unfuzzed/untrusted-input loaders by default. That is a direct, textbook match to A02's definition (insecure default / missing hardening step), not an analogy. Kept high; the draft already had this right.
rationale.a06_insecure_design: Accepting arbitrary user uploads and handing them to a native image library without an allowlist of vetted operations is a threat-model gap, not just a flippable setting -- same class as ImageTragick (2016), which the issue's own hint ladder cites at level 2. Overlaps conceptually with A02 (an insecure default is itself a design choice), which is exactly why this stays ambiguous rather than high: a reasonable grader could file it under either, and forcing a split would make the ground truth more confident than the category boundary actually is.
rationale.a03_software_supply_chain: Downgraded from the draft's `high` to `ambiguous`. libvips is a legitimate, intentionally-included dependency; the flaw is Rails' own configuration of it, not a compromised, unvetted, or tampered dependency entering the build. The A03 fit requires reading 'the application does not account for [dependency] risk' broadly enough to cover 'inherits a large native attack surface via many third-party codec libraries' -- defensible, but weaker than A02's direct CWE match, so it is not high.
rationale.a05_injection: Added as ambiguous (not in the draft). A crafted image file is untrusted data that ultimately drives unintended native code execution, which has injection-like shape (malicious input reaching an unintended execution path). But OWASP's Injection category is normally scoped to command/SQL/query interpretation, not memory-safety/parser exploitation in a native library -- so this is a plausible false-positive path for a grader to take, worth tracking as ambiguous rather than dismissing as clearly low.
rationale.low_categories: a01 (no access-control bypass or SSRF described), a04 (no cryptography involved), a07 (no identity/session handling involved), a08 (integrity failures normally connote unsigned/unverified updates, not input validation -- would double-count what a02/a06 already cover), a09 (advisory doesn't describe a detection/logging gap), a10 (this is a missing safety control, not fail-open exception handling per se -- weaker fit than a02/a06).
